tools.name: fetch_link_preview_metadata
tools.description: Fetches a web page from the given URL and returns its title, meta description and Open Graph image so a post preview can be shown before publishing.

params.name: url
params.description: URL of the page to preview

tools.code:
import re
import requests
from langchain_core.tools import tool


def _meta(html, prop):
    pattern = r'<meta[^>]+(?:property|name)=["\']' + re.escape(prop) + r'["\'][^>]*content=["\']([^"\']*)'
    m = re.search(pattern, html, re.I)
    return m.group(1) if m else None


@tool
def fetch_link_preview_metadata(url: str) -> dict:
    resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10, headers={"User-Agent": "SocialPreviewBot/1.0"})
    resp.raise_for_status()
    html = resp.text
    title = re.search(r"<title[^>]*>(.*?)</title>", html, re.I | re.S)
    return {
        "url": resp.url,
        "title": title.group(1).strip() if title else None,
        "description": _meta(html, "og:description") or _meta(html, "description"),
        "image": _meta(html, "og:image"),
    }

tools.name: import_post_image_from_url
tools.description: Downloads an image from a URL and saves it into the local media library folder so it can be attached to scheduled posts. Returns the saved file path and size.

params.name: image_url
params.description: URL of the image to download

params.name: filename
params.description: File name to save the image as in the media library

tools.code:
import os
import httpx
from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("media-library")

_LIBRARY_DIR = os.environ.get("MEDIA_LIBRARY_DIR", "./media_library")


@mcp.tool()
def import_post_image_from_url(image_url: str, filename: str) -> dict:
    os.makedirs(_LIBRARY_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    safe_name = os.path.basename(filename)
    with httpx.Client(timeout=20, follow_redirects=True) as client:
        resp = client.get(image_url)
        resp.raise_for_status()
    path = os.path.join(_LIBRARY_DIR, safe_name)
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(resp.content)
    return {"path": path, "bytes": len(resp.content), "content_type": resp.headers.get("content-type")}
